_meta.description: CBO-scored legislation used for fiscal accountability tracking. All deficit impacts are 10-year estimates relative to the CBO baseline at time of scoring. Positive = adds to deficit. Negative = reduces deficit.
_meta.scoring_convention: cbo_10yr_b: positive = adds to deficit (costs), negative = reduces deficit (saves). Figures are billions of dollars.
_meta.methodology: Each member's fiscal record is computed by summing CBO-scored impact of bills they voted Yea on. Voting Nay on a deficit-reducing bill is shown separately. No editorial weighting is applied — this is arithmetic on official government scores.

votes.name: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO/JCT scored the conference agreement at +$1,455B over 2018–2027. Including debt-service costs: ~$1,800B total impact.
votes.description: Permanently cut the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%; temporarily reduced individual income tax rates (expiring 2025); doubled the standard deduction.
votes.partisan_pattern: Near party-line: 51R yea / 48D-I nay in Senate; 224R yea / 201D nay in House

votes.name: Bipartisan Budget Act of 2018
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored +$320B over 10 years. Lifted Budget Control Act discretionary spending caps by $296B over FY2018–2019.
votes.description: Suspended the debt ceiling through March 2019 and raised discretionary spending caps by $296 billion over two years for both defense and non-defense programs.
votes.partisan_pattern: Bipartisan in Senate (71-28); mixed in House (167R+73D yea vs 67R+119D nay)

votes.name: CARES Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO/JCT estimated +~$1.7T over 2020–2030. Emergency COVID-19 response.
votes.description: Emergency pandemic relief: $1,200 direct payments, $600B+ in small business loans (PPP), expanded unemployment insurance, and $175B for hospitals and healthcare.
votes.house_vote_note: House passed by voice vote on March 27, 2020 — no recorded roll call exists.
votes.partisan_pattern: Unanimous in Senate (96-0). House: voice vote, no roll call.

votes.name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 — COVID Relief
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored the COVID-relief divisions (M & N) at ~$868B over 2021-2030: $184B in Div M + $682B in Div N. The full omnibus also contained FY2021 appropriations; only the COVID portion is attributed here, since trackers including CRFB treat the December 2020 package as the second major pandemic response after CARES.
votes.description: Second major pandemic relief package, attached to the FY2021 omnibus: $600 direct payments, $300/wk expanded unemployment, $325B small-business aid (incl. second-round PPP), $69B vaccine/testing, plus rental assistance and education aid. The bill also funded the federal government through FY2021.
votes.partisan_pattern: Strong bipartisan: 92-6 Senate; 359-53 House on the COVID-relief portion (Roll 251). A separate House vote (Roll 250, 327-85) covered the FY2021 funding portion.

votes.name: American Rescue Plan Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored +$1.9T over 2021–2031. Nearly all costs front-loaded in FY2021–2022.
votes.description: Pandemic relief: $1,400 direct payments, expanded child tax credit, $350B in state/local aid, vaccine distribution, and extended supplemental unemployment benefits.
votes.partisan_pattern: Near party-line: 50D-I yea / 49R nay in Senate; 220D yea / 211R+1D nay in House

votes.name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored +$256B net over 2021–2031. Includes $415B in new discretionary spending offset by $110B in mandatory savings and $50B in new revenues.
votes.description: Authorized $1.2 trillion for roads, bridges, broadband, rail, water systems, and electric vehicle infrastructure. Net deficit impact $256B after mandatory offsets.
votes.partisan_pattern: Bipartisan in Senate (50D+19R yea); mostly D in House (215D+13R yea vs 200R+6D nay)

votes.name: Honoring our PACT Act of 2022
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored the conference text at +$277B over 2022-2031: ~$278B in mandatory veterans-healthcare spending offset by ~$1B in revenues. Among the largest non-emergency mandatory expansions of the period.
votes.description: Expanded VA healthcare and disability benefits for ~3.5 million veterans exposed to toxic substances (burn pits, Agent Orange, radiation). Created a presumption-of-service-connection framework. Final law was enacted as S. 3373 after the House passed the Senate-amended bill on July 13, 2022 and the Senate concurred Aug 2, 2022.
votes.partisan_pattern: Bipartisan in both chambers: 86-11 Senate (Aug 2, 2022, after a procedural fight over a tax provision); 342-88 House (July 13, 2022).

votes.name: Inflation Reduction Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO/JCT's final post-enactment score: -$238B net deficit reduction over 2022–2031. (Initial Aug 3, 2022 estimate was -$305B; the final score reflects revisions to drug-pricing and energy-credit lines as enacted.) Revenue raisers: drug pricing reform, 15% minimum corporate tax, IRS enforcement funding. Offsetting outlays: clean-energy tax credits and extended ACA subsidies.
votes.description: Largest U.S. climate investment in history ($369B in clean energy credits) plus Medicare drug pricing reform; financed by a 15% minimum corporate tax, IRS enforcement funding, and other revenue measures.
votes.partisan_pattern: Party-line: 51D yea (inc. VP Harris tiebreak) / 50R nay in Senate; 220D yea / 207R nay in House

votes.name: Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023
votes.cbo_note: CBO projected -$1.5T over 2023–2033. IMPORTANT: ~$1.49T of savings are from discretionary spending caps that future Congresses must honor in annual appropriations. Hard mandatory/revenue savings: ~$10B. The cap savings are projections, not guaranteed.
votes.description: Debt ceiling suspension through January 2025 paired with discretionary spending caps for FY2024–2025, limits on unspent COVID funds, and mandatory program savings. CBO projected $1.5T in deficit reduction, primarily from the spending caps.
votes.partisan_pattern: Bipartisan: 149R+165D yea vs 71R+46D nay in House; 17R+46D-I yea in Senate

votes.name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored +$3.4T over 2025–2034 (vs. CBO Jan 2025 baseline). Breakdown: -$1.1T mandatory cuts (Medicaid, SNAP, student loans) offset by -$4.5T in revenue reductions (TCJA permanence + new cuts). Including debt service: ~$4.1T total impact.
votes.description: Made 2017 TCJA tax cuts permanent and added new reductions (no tax on tips/overtime, expanded deductions) while cutting Medicaid, SNAP, and student loan programs. CBO's largest single-bill deficit score in recent history.
votes.partisan_pattern: Near party-line: 50R yea + VP Vance / 50D-I nay in Senate; ~216R+2D yea vs all D + ~2R nay in House

votes.name: Families First Coronavirus Response Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO/JCT preliminary estimate (Apr 2, 2020): +$192B over the 2020-2030 period, mostly in FY2020-21. Emergency COVID-19 response.
votes.description: First major emergency pandemic package: free COVID-19 testing, paid sick and family leave for some workers, expanded unemployment benefits, and an increased federal Medicaid match (FMAP) for states.
votes.partisan_pattern: Strong bipartisan: 90-8 Senate; 363-40 House (all 40 nays were Republicans).

votes.name: Paycheck Protection Program and Health Care Enhancement Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO estimated +$483B over 10 years (per CRFB summary of the CBO score for H.R. 266). Gross spending: $484B in additional appropriations — PPP +$321B, hospitals +$75B, testing +$25B, plus administrative and EIDL components. Emergency COVID-19 response.
votes.description: Fourth COVID-19 emergency package ("COVID 3.5"): replenished the Paycheck Protection Program with $310B in additional small-business loans, added $75B for hospitals and healthcare providers, and $25B for testing.
votes.senate_vote_note: Senate passed by voice vote on April 21, 2020 — no recorded roll call exists.
votes.partisan_pattern: Senate: voice vote, no recorded roll call. House: 388-5 (the 5 nays were 4 Republicans — Massie, Biggs, Buck, Hice — and 1 Democrat, Ocasio-Cortez).

votes.name: Bipartisan Budget Act of 2019
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored a cap-driven net increase of ~$245B over 10 years: discretionary cap raises of $322B over FY2020-21 ($171B + $153B) partially offset by $77B in offsets ($16B from customs/passenger fee extensions and $62B from extending the mandatory sequester to 2029). The widely-cited '$1.7T addition to debt' figure includes cap extrapolation and interest; this entry uses the clean CBO net figure to match BBA 2018 methodology.
votes.description: Two-year debt ceiling suspension (through July 31, 2021) paired with discretionary spending cap increases for FY2020-21 ($322B above current law) and partial offsets.
votes.partisan_pattern: Bipartisan in both chambers: 67-28 Senate; 284-149 House.

votes.name: CHIPS and Science Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO scored mandatory + revenue effects at +$79B over 2022-2031 (+$48B over the first 5 years). Authorizations of an additional ~$200B in discretionary R&D and science funding are not counted in this score, since they require future appropriations. This entry uses the mandatory+revenue net figure to match the convention used for IIJA and IRA.
votes.description: Industrial policy package: ~$52B in semiconductor manufacturing subsidies and a 25% investment tax credit for chip fabs, plus ~$200B in authorized (not appropriated) R&D, STEM, and science programs over 10 years.
votes.partisan_pattern: Bipartisan: 64-33 Senate (47D-I + 17R yea); 243-187 House (24 R crossed over to support).

votes.name: Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015
votes.cbo_note: CBO 114th-Congress mandatory report (pub 52505) Table 2: outlays +$144.7B, revenues +$3.7B over 2015-2025 = +$141B net deficit increase. Repealed the Sustainable Growth Rate (SGR) formula governing Medicare physician payments and replaced it with a permanent payment update; CHIP 2-year reauth.
votes.description: Permanent repeal of the SGR formula governing Medicare physician payments, plus 2-year extension of CHIP and ~$70B in offsetting Medicare cost-sharing changes. Strong bipartisan vote.
votes.partisan_pattern: Strong bipartisan: 92-8 Senate; 392-37 House.

votes.name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016 / PATH Act
votes.cbo_note: CBO 114th-Congress mandatory report (pub 52505) Table 2: outlays +$157B, revenues -$523B over 2015-2025 = +$680B net deficit increase. PATH Act provisions (Division Q) drove the deficit impact; JCT JCX-143-15 scored the PATH tax provisions alone at +$622B in revenue loss over 10 years. House split the bill into two votes — Roll 703 covered the PATH Act tax provisions; we cite that as the policy-relevant House vote.
votes.description: Combined FY2016 omnibus appropriations with the Protecting Americans from Tax Hikes (PATH) Act, which made permanent many expiring tax provisions including the R&D credit, Section 179 expensing, and EITC/CTC enhancements.

house_roll_call.note: House split the bill into two votes; this is Roll 703 covering Division Q (PATH Act tax provisions). Roll 705 covered the omnibus appropriations portion.

votes.partisan_pattern: Senate 65-33; House PATH-portion 318-109.

votes.name: Social Security Fairness Act of 2023
votes.cbo_note: CBO cost estimate (Sep 9 2024, pub 60690): +$196B over 10 years. Repeals the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and the Government Pension Offset (GPO). Off-budget Social Security spending increase; brings forward trust-fund exhaustion by ~6 months.
votes.description: Repealed two Social Security provisions (WEP and GPO) that had reduced benefits for ~3 million public-sector retirees (teachers, firefighters, etc.) who also received non-covered pensions.
votes.partisan_pattern: Strong bipartisan: 76-20 Senate; 327-75 House.

votes.name: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.cbo_note: CBO 119th-1 mandatory report (pub 62240): +$66B over 10 years. Score is driven almost entirely by the rescission of $20.2B in IRS enforcement funding originally appropriated by IRA 2022 — CBO models reduced enforcement leading to lower compliance and lower revenue collections. METHODOLOGICAL NOTE: this is the same mechanism that earned P.L. 118-47 a +$38B score in 118-2 (which we excluded). We include this one because the rescission IS the substantive policy choice rather than an incidental rider — but the asterisk applies.
votes.description: Full-year continuing resolution funding the federal government through FY2025, paired with a rescission of $20.2B in IRS enforcement funding from IRA 2022.
votes.partisan_pattern: Near party-line: 54-46 Senate; 217-213 House.

votes.name: Build Back Better Act (House-passed version)
votes.cbo_note: CBO summary (Nov 18 2021, pub 57627): +$367B net deficit increase over 2022-2031. CRFB's widely-cited $2.4T figure is gross spending; CBO net (after revenue offsets) is +$367B. Passed House on Nov 19 2021; never received a Senate floor vote in BBB form. The H.R. 5376 bill number was later reused as the vehicle for IRA 2022 (separate score, separate vote).
votes.description: Sweeping climate, social, and tax package: universal pre-K, extended Child Tax Credit, ~$555B in climate investments, Medicare drug price negotiation, ACA subsidy expansion. Passed House 220-213 on party lines; died in the Senate when Sen. Manchin announced opposition.
votes.senate_vote_note: Never received a Senate floor vote in BBB form. The H.R. 5376 vehicle was later passed by the Senate as the Inflation Reduction Act (Aug 2022) with substantially different content and a separate score.
votes.partisan_pattern: Party-line in House: 220D yea / 212R + 1D nay. No Senate vote.

votes.name: American Health Care Act of 2017 (House-passed, post-MacArthur)
votes.cbo_note: CBO/JCT cost estimate (May 24 2017, pub 52752): net deficit reduction of $119B over 2017-2026 (direct spending -$1,111B, revenues -$992B). Coverage effect: 23M fewer insured by 2026. Earlier pre-MacArthur version (pub 52516) was scored at -$337B; we cite the post-MacArthur score because that's the version the House actually voted on.
votes.description: Republican plan to repeal and replace major portions of the ACA, including the individual mandate, expanded Medicaid, and the cost-sharing reduction subsidies. Passed House 217-213; never voted on the AHCA form in the Senate (the Senate pursued separate vehicles — see skinny_repeal_2017).
votes.senate_vote_note: Senate did not vote on the House-passed AHCA. Separate Senate ACA-repeal attempts are tracked under skinny_repeal_2017 (Healthcare Freedom Act).
votes.partisan_pattern: Party-line: 217R yea / 193D + 20R nay. No Democrats supported.

votes.name: Healthcare Freedom Act / 'Skinny Repeal' (S.Amdt. 667 to H.R. 1628)
votes.cbo_note: CBO score (pub 52979): net deficit reduction of $179B over 2017-2026. Senate-only attempt at partial ACA repeal — would have repealed the individual and employer mandates and the medical device tax. Failed 49-51 on Jul 28 2017 with McCain, Collins, and Murkowski voting nay.
votes.description: A bare-bones ACA partial-repeal package the Senate developed when the AHCA-equivalent and BCRA failed. Would have repealed the individual and employer mandates and the medical device tax while leaving the rest of the ACA intact. Famously defeated by John McCain's thumb-down vote at 1:30am.
votes.house_vote_note: Senate-only failed amendment; House did not vote on this version of H.R. 1628 (the House had previously passed the AHCA, scored separately).
votes.partisan_pattern: Near party-line: 49R yea (Collins, Murkowski, McCain nay) / 48D + 3R nay.

votes.name: Health and Economic Recovery Omnibus Emergency Solutions Act (H.R. 6800)
votes.cbo_note: CBO cost estimate (Jun 1 2020, pub 56383): +$3,397B net deficit increase over 2020-2030 (~$3.4 trillion). Largest single-bill score in the failed-bills set. House-Democrat COVID relief proposal; never received a Senate floor vote (Senate Republicans countered with the HEALS Act, which also never reached the floor). Many provisions later appeared at smaller scale in CAA Dec 2020 and ARPA 2021.
votes.description: House Democrats' second major COVID-19 relief package, following CARES. Would have provided ~$1T to state and local governments, expanded unemployment insurance, additional direct stimulus payments, and large education and healthcare provisions.
votes.senate_vote_note: Never received a Senate floor vote.
votes.partisan_pattern: Party-line in House: 207D + 1R yea / 14D + 185R nay.

votes.name: American Dream and Promise Act of 2021 (H.R. 6)
votes.cbo_note: CBO cost estimate (Apr 19 2021, pub 57068): +$30.6B net deficit increase over 2021-2031 (outlays +$34B, revenues +$3.4B). Just clears the $25B threshold. JCT did not issue a separate revenue score; CBO score covers both.
votes.description: Provided a path to lawful permanent residence and eventual citizenship for Dreamers (DACA-eligible), TPS holders, and DED recipients. Passed House 228-197; Senate took no floor action.
votes.senate_vote_note: Senate took no floor action. A companion bill (S. 264, Durbin) was never brought to the floor.
votes.partisan_pattern: Near party-line in House: 219D + 9R yea / 197R + 0D nay.

votes.name: Restoring Americans' Healthcare Freedom Reconciliation Act (H.R. 3762)
votes.cbo_note: CBO/JCT (Dec 11 2015, pub 51107): -$282B conventional net deficit reduction over 2016-2025 (-$474B with macroeconomic feedback; we cite the conventional figure to match the methodology used by the existing 14). ACA partial-repeal via budget reconciliation. Passed Senate 52-47, returned to House which concurred 240-181 on Jan 6 2016 (Roll 6). Vetoed by President Obama on Jan 8 2016. Override attempt failed 241-186 (short of 2/3) on Feb 2 2016.
votes.description: First reconciliation bill to actually pass both chambers attempting to repeal major portions of the ACA: Medicaid expansion, premium tax credits, the individual and employer mandates. Vetoed by Obama; the override attempt failed.

house_roll_call.note: Jan 6 2016 vote on motion to concur in Senate amendment — the version that went to the President. Earlier passage was Roll 568 (Oct 23 2015, 240-189), but we cite Roll 6 because it's the final form.

votes.partisan_pattern: Near party-line: 52R yea / 46D + 1R + 2I nay in Senate; 239R + 1D yea / 181D + 3R nay in House.
